title: Competitive Intelligence Report (illustrative sample, fictional competitors)

group.name: Meridian Legal AI
group.description: AI contract review for in-house legal teams.

group.name: Meridian Workflow
group.description: Sister company: contract lifecycle and approvals platform, same parent.

competitors.name: Clausewell
competitors.description: AI assistant inside Microsoft Word that reviews and redlines contracts.

competitors.name: Draftly
competitors.description: Contract drafting tool aimed at small and mid-size legal teams.

competitors.name: Northgate CLM
competitors.description: Enterprise platform for storing, approving and renewing contracts.

executive_summary: Bottom line: Clausewell and Northgate CLM both moved toward the same buyer this week, the in-house legal team that wants review, approval and renewal reminders in one place. That is the space our playbook product sells into, so expect more overlap in deals from Q4.

company_summaries.what_matters: Clausewell released Playbook Check on Sep 30, which compares a contract with a company's approved clauses inside Word at no extra cost. It does the same job as our playbook feature.
company_summaries.why: Buyers comparing the two will ask why they should pay extra for ours, so we need our own accuracy numbers and a clear answer on what happens after a clause is flagged.
company_summaries.title: Clausewell gives playbook review away in Word

company_summaries.what_matters: Northgate CLM added AI review inside its approval screen on Oct 1 and cut its Professional plan from $480 to $410 per user per year, about 15%.
company_summaries.why: It now sells review and approvals together for less, which puts deals where the customer already uses Northgate under the most pressure.
company_summaries.title: Northgate bundles AI review and approvals at a lower price

updates.what: On Sep 30 Clausewell released Playbook Check, which compares an incoming contract with a company's approved clause library and marks every difference as acceptable, risky or missing. It runs inside Word, takes about a minute for a 20-page contract, and is included in the Team plan at no extra cost. The company says early users cut first-pass review time by about 40%, though that figure comes from its own announcement.
facts: Released Sep 30, 2026; available to all Team and Enterprise customers
Included in the existing Team plan, so no price change
Works only inside Word; no web or Outlook version mentioned yet
40% faster first-pass review is the vendor's own claim, not independently checked
updates.why: This is the same job our playbook feature does, and Clausewell now gives it away inside a plan customers already pay for. Buyers comparing the two will ask why they should pay extra for ours, so we need a clear answer on accuracy and on what happens after the flag.
updates.response: Run our playbook check on the same 10 sample contracts and compare accuracy and speed, then prepare a one-page comparison for the sales team.

updates.what: On Oct 1 Northgate CLM added AI contract review directly inside its approval workflow, so a reviewer sees the AI's flagged risks next to the approve and reject buttons. On the same day it lowered its Professional plan from $480 to $410 per user per year, a cut of about 15%. It also published a customer story from a regional bank that says it now approves standard contracts in two days instead of five.
facts: AI review launched Oct 1, 2026 inside the approval screen
Professional plan now $410 per user per year, down from $480
Customer story: a regional bank went from 5 days to 2 days to approve standard contracts
updates.why: Northgate is going after the same in-house legal teams as us, with a lower price and a single tool for review and approval. Deals where the customer already uses a CLM system are the most exposed, because Northgate can now say it covers review as well.
updates.response: Ask the sales team to log every deal this month where Northgate comes up, and note whether price or the all-in-one pitch is the reason.

new_entrants.name: Pactline
new_entrants.note: Seed-stage startup that appeared in two searches this week. It says it reviews contracts by reading them against a customer's past negotiated deals. No customers or pricing are public yet, so there is nothing to act on, but check again in a month.

working_well.title: Review features that live inside the tool people already use
working_well.body: Clausewell inside Word and Northgate inside the approval screen both avoid asking people to open a new product. Both announcements lead with 'no new tool to learn', and Clausewell's customer quotes repeat it. The pattern suggests adoption, not features, is what these vendors are competing on.

working_well.title: Naming a concrete time saving
working_well.body: Northgate's regional bank story gives one number a buyer can repeat to a boss: 5 days down to 2. Clausewell gives 40%. Both are easier to sell than general claims about 'efficiency'. We do not yet publish a comparable number.

market_trends.title: Review is becoming a standard feature, not a product
market_trends.body: Two vendors in two different categories added contract review this week and neither charged extra for it. When a feature is bundled into existing plans, customers stop expecting to pay separately for it, so our pricing needs to be about the outcome (fewer risky contracts signed) rather than the review step itself.

market_trends.title: Price pressure is starting in the platform category
market_trends.body: Northgate's 15% cut is the first price move we have seen from a lifecycle platform this year. If other platforms follow, customers will compare our per-user price with theirs even though the products differ, so we should be ready with a simple explanation of what ours includes.

threats.title: Northgate bundles review and approvals at a lower price
threats.why: A customer who already needs approvals can now get review in the same product for 15% less than before, so the case for adding a separate review tool gets weaker.
threats.impact: Longer sales cycles and more discount requests in deals that include an existing Northgate user.

threats.title: Clausewell's Playbook Check matches our headline feature
threats.why: It does the same comparison against approved clauses, runs inside Word and costs nothing extra, though it is too new to know how accurate it is.
threats.impact: Buyers may stop treating playbook checking as something that deserves its own budget line.

opportunities.title: Show accuracy on real contracts
opportunities.body: Clausewell has published a speed claim but no accuracy numbers. A short, honest comparison of how often each tool catches a genuinely risky clause would give buyers a reason to look beyond price. We can run it on a neutral sample and publish the method.

opportunities.title: Position as the review layer that works with any platform
opportunities.body: Not every customer will move to Northgate, and many use a different system for storage and approvals. We can offer to sit on top of whichever platform they have, which Northgate cannot say.

actions.action: Run a head-to-head accuracy test against Clausewell's Playbook Check
actions.reason: We need our own numbers before sales is asked about it, and the vendor has not published any accuracy data.

actions.action: Brief the sales team on Northgate's new price and bundled review
actions.reason: Reps will meet this in live deals starting now and should know the three questions to ask the customer.

actions.action: Draft a one-page comparison of how we price versus bundled review
actions.reason: It gives sales a plain answer when a buyer says review is free elsewhere.
It is too early to judge, but a funded entrant targeting the same buyers is worth a second look.
